brief: UBS sales-and-trading flash covering two desks. Market internals (Cheong): expects $75-100bn of Risk Control Selling Monday, possibly continuing Tuesday, after which systematic selling should fade and set up a recovery. Despite Friday's sharp Nasdaq drop, excess sell-flow was only $8bn (Nasdaq) and -$24bn (SPX); retail reversed hard into the close, +$72bn of buying from 2:45pm, concentrated in Tech ETFs and Semis/Memory, Friday's worst performers. CTA selling drove 10 sell triggers Friday across ES1/NQ1/RTY1, but exposures have already fallen to the 19th/13th/15th percentile versus 3 years; only NQ1 retains active sell triggers, implying limited further CTA selling. Macro equity (Romano): October's funding-fear spike made it harder for incremental capital to reach Tech, with capex funding deals pulling money into credit instead; within equities this produced a broadening-out rotation, SPX equal-weight beating cap-weighted SPX by 6% in October despite hyperscaler earnings. Healthcare captured the rotation: XLV +23% in H2, half of it (+11%) in October alone, aided by defensive positioning plus AI/longevity growth exposure.
